title: Largest Odd Number in String
statement: The string `num` holds the decimal digits of a possibly huge non-negative integer. Among all non-empty contiguous pieces of `num`, consider those that, read as integers, are odd, and return the one with the greatest value as a string. If no piece is odd, return the empty string `""`.
notes:
## Intuition

An integer is odd exactly when its last digit is odd, so every odd piece ends at an odd digit. Let `end` be the position of the rightmost odd digit. Any odd piece ends at or before `end`, so it has at most `end + 1` digits. The prefix `num[0..end]` has exactly that many digits and starts with a non-zero digit, so no other odd piece can beat it. Trying every piece and comparing values works too, but it is quadratic and needs big-number arithmetic.

## Approach

1. Start `end` at the last index of `num`.
2. While `end` is still inside the string, read its `digit`.
3. If the digit is odd, stop: this is the rightmost odd digit.
4. Otherwise step `end` one place to the left.
5. Return the prefix up to and including `end`. When no odd digit exists, `end` is `-1` and the prefix is empty.

## Example 1, step by step

`num = "52"`. `end` starts at 1, where the digit is 2, which is even, so `end` becomes 0. The digit there is 5, which is odd, so the loop stops and the function returns `num.slice(0, 1) = "5"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each digit is looked at at most once, and the slice copies at most n characters.
- Space: O(n) for the returned string, O(1) otherwise.

## Pitfalls

- Do not convert `num` to a number: it can have 100,000 digits, far beyond any built-in integer type.
- Return the empty string, not `"0"` or `null`, when every digit is even.
- Scan from the right; the first odd digit from the left gives a far smaller answer (`"123456"` must give `"12345"`, not `"1"`).

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `end` | index being checked, moving left; finally the rightmost odd digit or `-1` |
| `digit` | numeric value of `num[end]` |

narration.2: Begin at the last digit, the one that decides whether a number is odd.
narration.3: Keep going while there are digits left to check.
narration.4: Turn the character at end into its numeric value.
narration.5: An odd digit here means the prefix ending at end is odd.
narration.6: It is the rightmost odd digit, so stop searching.
narration.8: An even digit cannot end an odd number; move one place left.
narration.10: Return the prefix through end; if no odd digit was found, end is -1 and this is the empty string.
